reason: अनु-उत्थित 'risen up to follow' is a valid participle describing the army ready to move, so the Gita Press reading stands.
रुद् is an adādi root whose feminine present participle is रुदती without nasal (Gita Press prints रुदती in the next verse too), so रुदत्यः is the regular form.
गुह् lengthens its vowel only before a vowel-initial suffix (6.4.89), so with ल्यप् the regular absolutive is उपगुह्य.
The thematic आसन्त is an ārṣa form Gita Press also prints at Bāla 14.18 (उपासन्ते); it is a recognised epic variant and the metre is intact.
सज्ज 'ready, equipped' is a valid and common epithet of a bow, so सज्जम् makes good sense beside सज्यम्.
अगुरु and अगरु are both standard forms of the aloe-wood name.
अनावृत 'uncovered, open' gives the same sense as अपावृत and is a valid word.
स्त्रीनिमित्तेन 'on account of a woman' is a valid compound that fits Bharata's being exiled through Kaikeyī.
The locative with प्रति-नी 'to lead back into Ayodhyā' is a valid construction in Gita Press's own form of the line, and the metre is complete.
Gita Press spells the apsaras's name अलम्बुषा consistently (also Bāla 47.12, Ayodhyā 91.47), a form MW records.
नागदत्ता is a valid name form for the apsaras, and nothing shows a slip.
फलभूषिताः 'adorned with fruits' is a valid compound with the same sense as फलभूषणाः.
Gita Press spells the apsaras's name अलम्बुषा consistently (also Bāla 47.12), a form MW records.
The augmentless plural उदीरयन् is an ārṣa imperfect Gita Press uses repeatedly (e.g. Ayodhyā 67.4, 91.60), so it is the edition's reading.
Sandal pastes kept 'in oceans' (samudra) makes no sense; the sense requires samudga 'caskets', as both sources read, so र is a typesetting slip for ग.
पादुकोपानहम् is the regular samāhāra-dvandva with the samāsānta टच् after a ह-final member (5.4.106, cf. छत्रोपानहम्), so the form is grammatical.
भ्रातुर्दर्शनलालसम् (genitive + compound) is a valid alternative to the compound भ्रातृदर्शनलालसम्.
अर्थवित् 'knower of the meaning' is a valid epithet of Bharadvāja, here qualifying the speaker.
द्विपवाजियूथा 'with herds of elephants and horses' is a valid compound that fits the army.
पृषतमुख्याः 'chiefly spotted deer' is valid and makes sense in the list of animals.
सम्परिश्रान्तवाहनः 'whose mounts were thoroughly tired' is a valid compound.
राज्यभ्रंशनम् 'loss of the kingdom' is a valid tatpuruṣa with the same sense as राज्याद्भ्रंशनम्.
Gita Press uses निष्पन्द for 'flow, trickle' elsewhere too (Kiṣkindhā 67.38, Uttara 28.43), and MW records the form in this sense, so it is the edition's reading.
Gita Press prints the same noun at Ayodhyā 24.34 (पितुरानृण्यताम्), so पितुश्चानृण्यता (च + आनृण्यता) is the edition's reading.
चन्द्रचारुनिभाननाम् 'whose face is like the lovely moon' is intelligible, and the metre is intact; only the order of the members differs.
पुष्पपत्राणि is the same dvandva with its members in the other order.
कल्मष and कलुष are synonyms, so विधूतकल्मषैः is a valid reading.
अश्वरथसम्पूर्णाम् 'full of horses and chariots' is a valid compound that makes sense.
हस्तिभिन्नम् 'split by an elephant' is a valid synonym of हस्तिभग्नम्.
धर्मनिश्चितः 'firm in dharma' is a valid epithet of Daśaratha.
Gita Press's line (उद्वेजिताः प्रजाः, राष्ट्रे तवावजानन्ति) is a coherent different reading, 'do the harassed people despise your ministers', with valid grammar.
कोष and कोश are both standard spellings of 'treasury'.
अदृष्टः 'unexamined' fits Gita Press's own form of this verse and is a valid word.
स्वर्गतिं पृथिवीपतेः 'the king's going to heaven' is grammatically consistent in Gita Press's line.
The augmentless imperfect अवतारयत् is an ārṣa form Gita Press also prints at Uttara 76.23, and the metre is intact.
उपगम्य 'having approached' is a valid absolutive with the same sense as उपागम्य.
जलापूरित 'filled with water' is a valid compound.
बदरैर्मिश्रम् 'mixed with jujube fruits' is valid and makes sense.
वाहान् परित्यज्य 'leaving their mounts' makes good sense in context.
खुरनेमिसमाकुलैः 'crowded with hooves and wheel-rims' is a valid compound.
इङ्गुदी is the standard feminine name of the tree, so इङ्गुदीक्षोद is a valid compound.
वनवासकृतां दीनां 'made dejected by forest life' is a possible reading and nothing proves a slip, so the edition's word stands.
अब्रतीत् is a non-word; the verb is अब्रवीत्, with त printed for व.
दुरावर (दुर् + आ-वृ + खल्, with guṇa) 'hard to check' is the regular Pāṇinian form.
उदकार्णवम् 'the ocean of water' is a valid compound in Gita Press's line (पूर्णं समुद्रम्).
समतिवर्तते 'goes beyond' gives good sense: no creature goes beyond its own nature.
धर्ममधर्मं च 'dharma and adharma' is a valid reading that makes sense.
परिगर्हे 'I censure' (ātmanepada) is a valid form, with अहम्.
यस्त्वम् 'you who spoke thus' is a valid relative construction.
अभिषिञ्चन is not a Sanskrit noun (MW and Apte have no such headword); the noun is अभिषेचन, which Gita Press itself prints in the same phrase at Ayodhyā 4.15.
प्रवाहये 'I carry on' is a valid causative with the same sense as प्रवर्तये.
शक्यतमः 'the one most able to be punished' fits Gita Press's own form of the line (स नास्तिके …), so it is the edition's reading.
अभ्यवदत् before प्रीतो is the correct sandhi for Gita Press's own form of the line.
शये 'I lie' (present for the near future) is a valid form in Gita Press's line.
उपाधि 'deceit, pretext' is a valid synonym of उपधि here.
कुलधर्मानुसंततम् 'continued as the family's dharma' agrees with धर्मम् in Gita Press's line.
The locatives नरव्याघ्रे … वरे agree with त्वयि in the same verse, so the reading is coherent.
अभ्युदितेन 'risen' describes the eclipsing planet validly.
युताम् 'joined with clouds' is a valid synonym of वृताम्.
निशाम्यते (passive of the causative of नि-शम् 'perceive', non-mit in this sense) is a regular form.
उत्कृष्ट 'drawn away' gives a possible sense in Gita Press's own form of the verse, and nothing proves a slip.
मार्गमार्यम् 'the noble path' (noun + adjective) has the same sense as आर्यमार्गम्.
गुरुवर्तिता 'the state of obeying the elder' is a valid abstract from गुरुवर्तिन्.
अवक्षिपन्ति 'they throw down' is valid and makes sense.
शारीरी is the regular feminine of the अण्-derivative शारीर (with ङीप्), so the form is correct.
युक्तस्य 'of one always devoted' is valid and fits the line.
Gita Press uses the infinitive बद्धुम् elsewhere (Araṇya 55.24, Sundara 50.16), so अवबद्धुम् 'to restrain' is the edition's form.
एतम् is a valid demonstrative beside anvādeśa एनम्.
वृत्तिवर्जितः 'without livelihood' fits Gita Press's own form of the line.
The feminine accusative उचितां has nothing to agree with; the sense 'what fitting and dear thing shall I do' (उचितं … प्रियं च किम्) needs neuter उचितं, as the other sources read.
प्रधर्षण is a valid neuter noun with the same meaning as प्रधर्षणा.
पतत्त्रिन् (from पतत्त्र 'wing') is a valid spelling MW records.
अल्पवर्णाः 'dim-coloured' trees at dusk is a valid reading that makes sense.
गभीर is a standard variant of गम्भीर.
सत्यवाञ्छीलवान् is the regular sandhi of न् + श.
ऋक्षाः 'bears' is a valid word that fits the list of beasts.
त्रैलोक्य is neuter only, so the accusative is त्रैलोक्यम्; त्रैलोक्याम् is an impossible form with an extra ा.
खण्ड is a valid synonym of षण्ड 'grove', so वनखण्ड makes sense.
महाराजतकोशः 'with a great silver scabbard' is a valid compound.
दैवत is also masculine (MW), so दैवतान् is valid, and the metre is intact.
तापसवेषेण 'in an ascetic's garb' is a valid synonym of तापसरूपेण.
The participle प्रपूजयन् 'honouring' is a valid elliptical construction in Gita Press's own form of the line.
मानवौ 'two men' is a valid synonym of मानुषौ.
निरर्थिका is the regular feminine of निरर्थक (इत् before आप्, 7.3.44).
मृत्योर्वश्यः 'in death's power' is valid and has the same sense as the compound.
कनीयाँल्लक्ष्मणः is the regular न् + ल sandhi.
कर्षित 'tormented' is a valid synonym of कर्शित here.
सकुशलम् 'in good health' is a valid word.
राजँल्लोकानाम् is the regular न् + ल sandhi.
The plural महानादान् 'great roars' is valid.
तदा 'then' is a valid alternative to तथा.
क्रोधन 'irascible' is a valid synonym of क्रोधिन्.
लोष्ठ is a recognised spelling of लोष्ट 'clod' (MW).
परिकीर्तितांस्तथा 'thus proclaimed' is a valid reading.
फलिनाम् 'of fruit-bearing trees' is a valid reading that makes sense.
